Subject: Helix MAP: performance benchmarking plan and initial schedule

Hi Beth / Helix Ops team,

Per our MAP, attached is the proposed benchmarking plan for the three hosting modes we discussed (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pool, Private/VPC). High level goals:

- Validate latency targets across typical request shapes (short chat turn, long context completion)
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token), steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), and p50/p95/p99 latency at target concurrencies
- Characterize autoscale behaviors (warm/cold start, ramp times) and isolation variance under background noise
- Produce a concise results appendix you can include in your MAP and procurement packet

Planned test matrix (attached worksheet):
- Workloads: 4 canonical prompts (chat short ~40 tokens, assistant reply ~120 tokens, long completion 1024 tokens, embedding-ish bulk)
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 128 parallel requests
- Metrics: TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rate, memory pressure (KV cache hits)
- Variants: kernel quantized model, full fp16 model; KV cache on/off for subsequent calls

Schedule (proposed):
- Test harness handoff & config (we provide): Tue 2027-06-29
- Dry run (low concurrency): Wed 2027-06-30 AM
- Full sweep (all modes): Wed 2027-06-30 PM
- Results review & MAP update: Thu 2027-07-01

Attachments: map-helix-benchmark-plan.xlsx, test-harness-config.json

Questions for you now: any compliance constraints for test data (PII/drug codes), and do you want us to exercise your Private cluster via a VPN jump or will you run the harness inside your VPC?

Thanks — aiming to keep this tightly scoped so we can lock the MAP milestones.

—Naomi

Looping in Marcus and Rishi for the implementation details on the test harness and acceptance criteria. Short checklist for the run:

Acceptance criteria (what we will sign off in MAP review):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for short-chat path at concurrency 8 under Dedicated; p95 <= 350ms hosted (best-effort)
- TTFT: <= 130ms for Dedicated, reasonable variance allowed for Hosted (<= 220ms)
- Throughput: able to sustain >2000 tokens/sec at concurrency 32 on Dedicated using quantized model
- Errors: <0.5% error rate across runs
- Autoscale: ramp to steady capacity within 90s for Hosted (observed), near-instant for Dedicated (reserved pool), Private dependent on cluster autoscaler but target < 120s

Test harness notes (Marcus / Rishi action items):
- Provide the containerized client and a runbook (Marcus) — include env vars to pin model variant and KV cache toggles.
- Produce a small script to toggle synthetic background noise (Rishi) to test noisy-neighbor isolation for Hosted.
- Capture metrics to CSV with headers: timestamp, endpoint, mode, concurrency, TTFT_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_sec, errors, kv_cache_hit_rate

Schedule (confirmed):
- Marcus to share container + runbook by EOD 6/29
- Dry run 6/30 09:00-11:30 PT (Helix will run inside their VPC for Private checks)
- Full sweep 6/30 13:00-17:00 PT
- MAP results review call 7/01 10:00 PT (30 min)

Mapping to MAP milestones: if results meet criteria we will move to term sheet milestone (close target 2027-08-15). If we fail to meet key latencies, we will provide optimization recommendations (batching, quantization tweaks, prefix caching) and a follow-up 1-week retest.

Team — quick note after the full sweep today (attached CSV: latency-results-20270630.csv). We ran the three hosting modes and the results below are our consolidated observations (short-chat path, 120-token response):

- Hosted API (multi-tenant): p50 95ms, p95 320ms, p99 560ms at concurrency 32. TTFT observed ~140ms. Throughput ~2100 tokens/sec. Autoscale ramp ~70s; variance higher when background noise injected.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): p50 88ms, p95 160ms, p99 200ms at concurrency 32. TTFT ~105ms. Throughput ~2450 tokens/sec. Predictable, minimal variation across repeats.
- Private (Helix VPC): p50 90ms, p95 170ms, p99 350ms at concurrency 32. TTFT ~120ms. Throughput ~2300 tokens/sec. Autoscale ramp depended on cluster config (~120s) and showed some variance tied to node provisioning.

Notes / implications for MAP:
- Dedicated gives the best predictability and highest steady throughput; good fit for our SLA-focused path in the MAP.
- Hosted is easiest operationally but shows higher p99 variance; acceptable for dev / low-SLA routes.
- Private matched Dedicated closely on central metrics but autoscale behavior and node provisioning are Helix responsibilities — include a MAP item to validate cluster autoscaler tuning and pre-warm strategy.

Action items for the MAP update (Beth / Naomi / Karthik):
- Naomi to update MAP milestones to mark Dedicated as the recommended production mode for SLA-heavy traffic (update due: 7/02)
- Helix Ops to validate cluster autoscaler pre-warm window and provide expected node spin-up times (due: 7/06)
- Redwood (Marcus/Rishi) to provide a short optimization plan if Helix wants Dedicated-like predictability on Hosted (batching profiles, prefix caching best-practices) — deliverable by 7/05

Attachments: latency-results-20270630.csv (CSV of raw runs), test-harness-config.json (run parameters)

We are aligned to proceed with the MAP updates and target the 2027-08-15 close if the actions above are completed. Thanks for a smooth run.

—Beth
